anomalies.observed: J11 is a 2-pin screw terminal on the Microcontroller sheet. Pin 2 is connected to the heater control net (/Microcontroller/NET0011, which includes U2.GPIO1, U4.IN, and U4.DIAG_EN), and pin 1 is connected to GND. This net also drives the heater switch input and a status LED, but it is not the switched heater output.
anomalies.expected: No screw terminal should directly bridge an MCU output/control net to GND. The heater connector should be on the switched high-side output (U4.OUT), as seen on J1. The specification lists J11 as the barrel jack, but in this netlist the barrel jack is J7, so J11 is an extra connector not present in the intended design.

evidence.quote: heater output net through a smart high-side switch (U6, TPS1H200AQDGNRQ1) switched from ESP32's GPIO1 ... OUT (pin 7) feeds the heater connector J6 pin 2

anomalies.impact: If a user connects a heater or any shorting device to J11, it will short the ESP32 GPIO1 and the TPS1H200 input to GND, disabling the heater and potentially damaging the GPIO. Even left open, it is an unintended connector on a sensitive control net.

parsed.summary: The design files contain an extra screw terminal J11 that ties the heater control net (ESP32 GPIO1 / TPS1H200 IN and DIAG_EN) to GND. This is not part of the specified design and creates a risk of shorting the control line, disabling the heater and potentially damaging the MCU.
